clue.text: What's left stays

definitions.meaning: the leftovers or residue of something, a noun sense
continues to be present, a verb sense

explanation.surface: A remark that whatever is left over is staying put.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses of one word: leftover remnants as a noun, and the verb meaning to stay behind.

clue.text: May cover you, by the sound of it

definitions.text: May cover you, by the sound of it

parts.words: May cover you, by the sound of it
parts.note: read 'you' as the female sheep it sounds like: a woolly coat is what covers that animal

explanation.surface: A garment that might be worn over you, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'You' is said like 'ewe', a female sheep, and a sheep's woolly coat covers the ewe.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheep's woolly coat is what covers a ewe, the word that 'you' sounds like.

clue.text: One out to arouse a soldier of the reserves to take a hill…

parts.note: GI is an American private soldier
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's reserve force
a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A troublemaker recruits a reservist to storm a hilltop.
explanation.walkthrough: The TA (Territorial Army) is the British army's volunteer reserve; a tor is a rocky hilltop in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: A stirrer-up of discontent sets out to rouse people to action.

clue.text: And swamp a doctor, getting a gunner to take ship

parts.note: MO is a medical officer
RA is the Royal Artillery, so a gunner
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: A medic and an artilleryman board a vessel and get bogged down.
explanation.walkthrough: RA, the Royal Artillery, stands for a gunner in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: A bog or marsh, wet ground in which one gets stuck, is a synonym.

clue.text: Hardened to customers' pleas in the laundry!

definitions.text: Hardened to customers' pleas in the laundry!

parts.words: Hardened to customers' pleas in the laundry!
parts.note: seems to be a hard-hearted laundry deaf to complaints; really, shirts stiffened as customers asked

explanation.surface: Laundry staff have grown deaf to complaints from their clientele.
explanation.definitionFit: Collars stiffened with a laundry stiffening agent, as many customers once requested, are hardened.

clue.text: Barber's cabin staff reduction?

definitions.note: a style a barber gives, a noun phrase for the haircut

parts.note: a ship's or plane's crew
a cut is a reduction

explanation.surface: A barber's term for trimming the number of flight attendants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barber's' stands for a barber's work, the very short haircut, so the possessive is a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A very short haircut is a familiar style given at a barber's shop.

clue.text: Found by sailors to stop illness on board

definitions.text: Found by sailors to stop illness on board

parts.words: Found by sailors to stop illness on board
parts.note: sounds like a seasickness remedy; really the steadiness sailors acquire after time afloat

explanation.surface: A remedy discovered by mariners to prevent seasickness.
explanation.definitionFit: Sailors acquire the ability to keep balance on a rolling deck, which keeps them from feeling sick.

clue.text: Our pet's wrong attitude

indicators.note: wrong suggests the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: Complaining that the family pet's behaviour is bad.
explanation.definitionFit: A bodily stance or a mental stance, both meanings of attitude.

clue.text: Mark the bill

definitions.meaning: to scratch or notch a line

explanation.surface: Make a note of the restaurant bill.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: to scratch a line, and a reckoning owed, as in paying off old debts.

clue.text: Like King James version before nearly all the credit has been given

indicators.note: a new version of a name hints at the letters reworked
drop the final letter, leaving most of the word

parts.note: on tick means on credit

explanation.surface: A remark about the King James Bible and paying for it on credit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'version' rearranges JAMES to MAJES; 'nearly all' cuts TICK (credit, as in 'on tick') to TIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Regal, dignified, as befits a monarch.

clue.text: Flew against the enemy in wars or revolutions

definitions.note: a phrase for things that flew at the foe, standing for the missiles themselves

indicators.note: revolutions turn things around, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Something launched at the foe in conflicts and uprisings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutions' rearranges WARSOR. The definition is a description, 'what flew against the enemy'.
explanation.definitionFit: Archers' missiles were shot through the air at opposing troops.

clue.text: Speculator may lay siege to something

definitions.meaning: what a speculator may do with money: put it into stocks
an old military sense, to surround a town

explanation.surface: A financier might besiege some target.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: putting money into a venture, and the old military meaning of surrounding a fortress.

clue.text: Time travellers can mostly be found in it!

definitions.text: Time travellers can mostly be found in it!

parts.words: Time travellers can mostly be found in it!
parts.note: suggests science-fiction time travel; really the busy period when most commuters are on the move

explanation.surface: A science-fiction hint at where chrononauts gather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Time travellers' looks like a sci-fi phrase; split it as 'Time' then 'travellers'.
explanation.definitionFit: The peak commuting period is when most people are travelling.

clue.text: Of course it's to plot

definitions.meaning: a navigator's map shows a vessel's course
to map out or record on paper

explanation.surface: Naturally, the aim is to scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of course' looks like 'naturally'; read it as a ship's course.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea map traces a course, and to map is to plot a route.

clue.text: To make it 3-1,we hear, without a break

definitions.text: To make it 3-1,we hear, without a break

parts.words: To make it 3-1,we hear, without a break
parts.note: three in one go: three successive goals or wickets with no interruption

explanation.surface: A sports report on scoring to go 3-1 up without pause.
explanation.definitionFit: Three successes in a row by one player, uninterrupted, as in cricket or football.

clue.text: Goes round one of the hazards to divers

definitions.text: one of the hazards to divers
definitions.meaning: decompression sickness, from surfacing too fast

explanation.surface: Someone circles one of the dangers facing scuba enthusiasts.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: curves round, and decompression sickness suffered by divers who surface too quickly.

clue.text: Greet a Russian fighter about to get a minute measuring device!

indicators.note: about signals the letters are moved around

parts.note: MiG is a Russian fighter plane

explanation.surface: Welcoming a Soviet jet pilot before handing over a clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges GREET plus MIG (a Soviet jet).
explanation.definitionFit: A small sand-glass timing a few minutes for boiling breakfast.

clue.text: Officer appointed to check unusual loss of life

definitions.text: Officer appointed to check unusual loss of life

parts.words: Officer appointed to check unusual loss of life
parts.note: an official holding inquests into sudden or suspicious deaths

explanation.surface: A job description for an official investigating strange deaths.
explanation.definitionFit: This official holds inquests into deaths that are sudden, violent or unexplained.

clue.text: Work from the Bible and quietly distribute charity

parts.note: p is piano, quietly in music

indicators.note: distribute spreads things about, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: alms are charity given to the poor

explanation.surface: Read scripture and hand out donations without fuss.
explanation.definitionFit: A sacred song from the Old Testament collection is a biblical composition.

clue.text: Peradventure, prude leaves out an old soldier

indicators.note: leaves out takes one word's letters from another, and out signals the remainder is mixed

explanation.surface: Perhaps a prim person ignores an elderly ex-serviceman.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the letters of PRUDE from PERADVENTURE ('perhaps'), leaving AVENTRE, then 'out' rearranges them.
explanation.definitionFit: An experienced ex-serviceman, long in military service, is a synonym.

clue.text: Badly gas those held by the enemy, to ensure good behaviour

definitions.text: held by the enemy, to ensure good behaviour
definitions.note: describes the people so held, standing for the captives themselves

indicators.note: done badly, the letters are put in disorder

explanation.surface: A grim call to gas prisoners of war.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Badly' rearranges GASTHOSE. 'those' does double duty only in the surface: the definition reads as 'those held'.
explanation.definitionFit: Captives kept as security by a foe so that the other side behaves.

clue.text: Do the groundwork on a plot

definitions.text: Do the groundwork on a plot

parts.words: Do the groundwork on a plot
parts.note: sounds like preparing a story; literally tending the ground of a patch of land

explanation.surface: Lay the foundations for a novel's storyline.
explanation.definitionFit: To tend flower beds and vegetables is working the soil of a plot.

clue.text: One who cleans fish by the side of the road

definitions.meaning: someone who removes a fish's innards
the channel along a road's edge

explanation.surface: A fishmonger working at the roadside.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a person who guts fish, and the drainage channel at a kerb.

clue.text: Practically nothing but speculation

parts.note: almost entirely guesswork; also, what has nothing to do with practice

explanation.surface: A dismissal of an idea as almost pure guesswork.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Practically' seems to mean 'almost'; read it as 'in practice', the opposite of conjecture.
explanation.definitionFit: A hypothesis or conjecture is the opposite of practice.

clue.text: Describes a repugnant sensation

parts.note: a word naming a feeling of intense dread and disgust

explanation.surface: A dictionary-style gloss on a revolting feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: Intense fear mixed with loathing is a feeling of repugnance.

clue.text: Hung about the Spanish editor for a change

indicators.note: a change of order rearranges these letters

parts.note: el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: Someone lingered near the Spanish newspaper editor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for a change' rearranges EL plus EDITOR.
explanation.definitionFit: To dawdle or linger aimlessly is to hang about.

clue.text: Working class supervisor

parts.note: seems to be a blue-collar foreman; really one who works overseeing a school class

explanation.surface: A foreman from a blue-collar background.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Working class' looks like a social label; read 'working' and 'class supervisor' separately.
explanation.definitionFit: A schoolteacher's job is to be in charge of a class of pupils.

clue.text: Ordered by a judge to get a second opinion!

definitions.text: Ordered by a judge to get a second opinion!

parts.words: Ordered by a judge to get a second opinion!
parts.note: sounds like a medical referral; really a fresh court hearing before a new jury

explanation.surface: A judge's instruction to consult another doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: A fresh hearing of a case, ordered by the court, gives a new verdict.
